content.summary: The four-star correction survives the j=4 challenge, and its four-unit penalty is valid for distinct rank-four members. Frozen hashes match; I read the committed changes. No theory revision is required by this focused check.

checks.method: Enumerated j=0 through 4 exactly, tested two rank-five sets intersecting in all four selected points, and inspected FourStar's distinctness hypotheses.
checks.observation: The correction values are 0,0,1,2,2. At j=4, intersection excess is at least 3, so no omitted quadruple term is needed for this lower bound. Distinct rank-four members actually cannot have j=4. Three distinct four-sets containing one selected triple have distinct fourth points and form a sunflower; hence each triple-codegree is at most two. Four selected triples therefore contribute at most four binomial penalties. Repeated selected points or empty intersections would invalidate the general pointwise lemma, and its hypotheses exclude both.
